summary: Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Nagoya University. She has held posts at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. She studied at the University of Chicago and under D. T. Suzuki, Sokei-an, Zuigan Goto, and Mukai Kono. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America and abbess of Ryōsen-an.

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University under John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She has held research posts at the Australian National University and the University of Munich.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi, and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis.

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA in Religious Studies at Naropa University. He studied under teachers including Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and Sarah Harding, alongside several traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brown and Harvard universities and has held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley, and Wesleyan University.
Ryo Kuroiwa is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He has held appointments at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University around 1991–1995 and under Fumihiko Sueki between roughly 1996 and 2004.
Ryōshō Taira was a Buddhist studies scholar who held academic posts at Taisho University, including being attested as professor emeritus in 1976.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a full-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University.

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and the Humboldt University of Berlin under teachers including Shun'ichi Takagi. He lectured at Humboldt University and served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1953 to 1978.
Ryoichi Kondo was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University.

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryojin Soga was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shinshu and Otani universities and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University and Otani University, where he was also president from 1961 to 1967.
Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College and as a faculty professor of social welfare at Rissho University.
Ryojun Okubo was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Morito Ninomiya and held a post at Taisho University.
Ryokei Kaginushi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters at Otani University.
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University and as a lecturer at Osaka University.
Ryoko Mochizuki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1958 to 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University.
